why: Prefix of a mod: a subarray sum is divisible by k exactly when the two prefix sums around it have the same remainder mod k. Count remainders in a hash map (or an array of size k) as you sweep; each earlier prefix with the same remainder is one more subarray.
hints: Write the subarray sum as P[j] - P[i]. When is that divisible by k?
When P[j] mod k == P[i] mod k. So you are counting pairs of prefixes with equal remainders.
count[0] = 1; s = 0; for each x: s = (s + x) mod k (non-negative), answer += count[s], count[s] += 1. O(n + k).
pitfalls: Negative values: normalise the remainder to [0, k) (Python's % already does).
Seed count[0] = 1 for subarrays that start at index 0.
